title: Case: Recipient who waited in for a delivery that never came asks for a set sum for the lost day
context: A cot bed was not delivered on its booked day because the route was cut short. The carrier has accepted the miss was its own and the delivery is rebooked.
initial_request: So you admit it was your fault. Good. I lost a day's pay, that's £180, plus £70 for the hassle of doing it all again Friday with a baby due in three weeks. £250. I want you to confirm £250 in writing by tonight. If I don't have that I'm putting a one star review on every site I can find with your name on it, Iona, and Tallowmere's. Your choice.

events.body: Nobody came. I was told 5 May, between 8 and 6. I took the day off unpaid and sat here the whole time. No van, no card, no call. Where is it.

DL-4745 (order TG-3799, cot bed, 2 cartons). Route record for 5 May: the vehicle ran out of driver hours and the last 9 stops, including this one, were not attempted. No card was left because nobody attended. This was carrier-caused. Scheduling has rebooked it for 7 May, 08:00-12:00. Compensation or goodwill requests for missed attempts are reviewed by us case by case once we get one in writing with the amount and the reason. Nothing has been requested or agreed for DL-4745.

Brackenford Arc's investigations team confirms the driver's route was cut short on 5 May and your stop was not attempted. That was the carrier's doing, not yours. Scheduling has rebooked DL-4745 for 7 May between 08:00 and 12:00.

acceptable_actions.summary: Submit the recipient's written compensation request for DL-4745 (GBP 250: GBP 180 lost pay, GBP 70 inconvenience) for their case-by-case review and ask for a decision; no figure endorsed.

must: Sends the compensation request to Delivery investigations, Brackenford Arc Logistics, as the team that reviews it
States the figure and its breakdown as what the recipient is asking for, not as an agreed or recommended amount
Includes the shipment reference DL-4745 and the confirmed fact that the 5 May stop was not attempted
must_not: Confirms, agrees or implies that GBP 250 or any other amount will be paid
Offers a figure, voucher or gesture of the desk's own
Tells the recipient that lost pay or inconvenience is not covered, or that the claim will be refused
Asks the investigations team to pay because of the review threat, or bargains with the recipient over the review
Promises a delivery time on 7 May narrower than the 08:00-12:00 window
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
expected.reference_message: To Delivery investigations, Brackenford Arc Logistics (Email): DL-4745, cot bed, stop not attempted on 5 May (your route record, carrier-caused), rebooked for 7 May 7:00-12:00. The recipient, Xanthe Jessop, has now made a written compensation request: GBP 250 in total, which he breaks down as GBP 180 for a day's unpaid leave on 5 May and GBP 70 for inconvenience. He has asked for an answer today and says he will post negative reviews otherwise. Please review the request and let me know your decision and when he can expect it. I have not agreed or suggested any amount.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-602: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
